sections.body: Letters make sounds. To read a new word, say each sound and blend them: c-a-t → cat!
Some letters team up: 'sh' in ship, 'ch' in chip, 'th' in thin.
Some words are tricky and don't follow the rules, like 'the', 'said' and 'was'. We learn these by sight.
Sound out: d-o-g, f-i-sh, s-u-n. What words did you make?
Point under each sound as your child blends. Short, daily practice (5–10 minutes) beats long sessions.

quiz.q: Blend the sounds: s-h-i-p. What word is it?
hints: 'sh' is the sound you make to say 'be quiet'.

quiz.q: Which word is a 'tricky word' you learn by sight?
hints: One of them doesn't sound like its letters (s-a-i-d isn't 'sed').
'was' sounds like 'woz', not w-a-s. Find another word like that.
quiz.explain: 'said' doesn't follow the sound rules, so we learn it by sight.

quiz.q: Which word starts with the 'ch' sound?
hints: Say each word out loud. Listen to the start.
'ch' sounds like the end of a sneeze: a-CHOO!
'shop' starts with 'sh', like 'shh, be quiet'. Now find the 'ch' word.
